comments.note: In matchRoute(), the existing GET /api/projects/:slug routes (plan, synthesis, health, work-packages) decode the slug from rest[1] without decodeURIComponent — they use rest[1]! directly. The new runs routes use decodeURIComponent(rest[1]!) for consistency with how the PATCH and POST routes decode slugs in handleRequest(). This is correct behaviour but there is a latent inconsistency in the older routes. A follow-up pass to harmonise all slug decoding in matchRoute() would improve consistency.

This is acceptable for the current use-case but worth documenting if live config reloading is ever required for this field.

summary: BLOCKING: `instanceof ApiError` check in server.ts will silently swallow run-log errors as 500s.

The `ApiError` class in `src/gui/log-resolver.ts` is a separate class from the `ApiError` imported by `server.ts` from `./api.js`. JavaScript `instanceof` checks identity of the constructor — two structurally identical classes in different modules are not the same class.

Consequence: any `ApiError` thrown by `handleListRunLogs` or `handleGetRunLog` (e.g. NOT_FOUND for a bad slug via `assertSafeSlug()`, FORBIDDEN for path-traversal attempts in `readLogEntries()`, NOT_FOUND for a missing log file) will fall through the `else` branch in server.ts's error handler, log to stderr as 'Unhandled error', and return a 500 response to the client instead of the correct 403 or 404.

Fix options (in order of preference): (1) Extract `ApiError` to a shared `src/gui/errors.ts` module and import from there in both `api.ts` and `log-resolver.ts`. (2) Change the `instanceof` guard in server.ts to a duck-type check: `err instanceof Error && typeof (err as any).code === 'string'`. Option 1 is preferred — it resolves the architectural duplicate noted in the module-level comment of log-resolver.ts and eliminates the latent risk for any future `src/gui/` utility that needs to throw structured errors.

No existing test exercises the server's HTTP error mapping for these routes (only the underlying resolver functions are unit-tested in isolation). A test that calls the HTTP server with a bad slug or filename and asserts a 404/403 status code would have caught this.

All other aspects of the implementation are correct: route registration logic is sound, segment-count discrimination prevents shadowing, `afterLine` parsing is correct, logsDir closure is correct, TypeScript types are satisfied, and the security guards in `readLogEntries()` are thorough.

comments.note: BLOCKING — instanceof ApiError mismatch causes run-log errors to be returned as HTTP 500. `server.ts` imports ApiError from `./api.js` (gui/api.ts). The run-log handlers import ApiError from `src/gui/log-resolver.ts`. These are two distinct classes. The `err instanceof ApiError` guard at lines 440, 456, 481, 513, and 535 of server.ts will always evaluate to false for errors thrown from handleListRunLogs or handleGetRunLog. All structured ApiError responses (NOT_FOUND for invalid slug, FORBIDDEN for path traversal, NOT_FOUND for missing file) will be caught by the else-branch, emitting a stderr log and returning a 500 to the client. Fix: create a shared `src/gui/errors.ts` exporting the single ApiError class, then import it in both `gui/api.ts` and `src/gui/log-resolver.ts`.

No integration test covers the HTTP-level error mapping for the new run-log routes. The existing tests in `tests/gui/log-resolver.test.ts` test the underlying functions in isolation and would not catch the instanceof mismatch. A test that spins up the real server (or calls handleRequest directly) and asserts that a request with an invalid slug returns 404, and a request with a path-traversal filename returns 403, should be added to `tests/gui/run-log.test.ts` (currently that file tests only the client-side JS).

LATENT (pre-existing, noted by Developer): The slug in the GET /api/projects/:slug/runs and GET /api/projects/:slug/runs/:filename routes is decoded via decodeURIComponent(rest[1]!), but the older sibling routes (plan, synthesis, health, work-packages at rest.length=3) use rest[1]! directly without decoding. This inconsistency means a URL-encoded project slug would be handled differently by the two route groups. Should be normalised in a follow-up pass across all matchRoute() branches.

LATENT (pre-existing): `afterLine` query param is parsed with parseInt(afterParam, 10) without validation for NaN or negative values. If `?after=-5` or `?after=abc` is passed, afterLine will be NaN or -5. In readLogEntries(), the guard `afterLine != null && afterLine > 0` correctly treats NaN and negative values as 0 (skip nothing), so this does not cause incorrect behaviour — but an explicit validation at the parse site would be more defensive and self-documenting.

The module-level Known Limitations comment in `src/gui/log-resolver.ts` notes that `resolveOrchestratorLogsDir` and `findRunLogs` do not validate that the path is absolute. Now that these are wired into the HTTP server, the Documentation agent should ensure this limitation is surfaced in the developer guide / API surface doc for the run-log feature, alongside the planned fix (add path.isAbsolute() guard in resolveOrchestratorLogsDir).
